presets.label: Miniature — high detail
presets.summary: Small display piece. Detail beats speed; supports allowed.

prompt.parametric:
INTENT PRESET: MINIATURE — HIGH DETAIL.
Target: a small display object printed on a Bambu P1S with a 0.4 mm nozzle at 0.08 mm layers.

Resolution: set $fa = 2 and $fs = 0.2 at the top of the file. Never set a global $fn.
Fastener or bearing bores, if any, get an explicit $fn = 64.

Minimum printable geometry — treat these as hard floors, not suggestions:
  - free-standing protrusion (finger, spike, antenna, blade): >= 1.0 mm thick
  - solid wall: >= 0.8 mm
  - raised relief: >= 0.6 mm wide, 0.3-0.6 mm proud
  - engraved relief: >= 0.6 mm wide, >= 0.4 mm deep
  - gap between two details: >= 0.6 mm
  - NO knife edges. Every terminating edge is truncated to a >= 0.5 mm flat or a 0.3 mm chamfer.
    A sub-0.42 mm edge is narrower than one extrusion and prints as a ragged blob.
Detail finer than the nozzle cannot exist. Stylise up: make features chunkier and more
deliberate rather than finer. Chunky detail reads well on FDM; delicate detail disappears.

Do not model: wispy hair, thin swords or spear tips, sub-1 mm chains, trailing unsupported
cloak edges, free-floating elements. If the concept needs one, either thicken it 2-3x or
emit it as a separate part on the same plate.

Supports ARE allowed for this preset (tree/organic, Z-distance 0.2 mm) - detail beats
supportlessness here. Orient the piece tilted 15-20 degrees backward so layer lines fall on
the back, not the face, and put the most detailed surface facing up. Bases print flat with a
5 mm brim.

Colour every part with color(). Add a bottom chamfer of 0.4 mm x 45 degrees where the model
meets the bed. Keep the model manifold; overlap coincident-height neighbours by eps = 0.01.

generated.image_suffix:
Single centred subject on a plain seamless light-grey background, even soft diffused
lighting from the front-upper-left with no harsh shadows and no strong rim light, full
subject visible with clear margin on all sides, sharp focus throughout, no depth-of-field
blur. Three-quarter view. Sculptural collectible-figure look: bold simplified forms and
chunky deliberate detail, clean readable silhouette, features exaggerated slightly larger
than life so they survive at small scale. Matte unpainted grey resin/clay finish, one
uniform colour. Reproduce a real physical object - do NOT invent, add, extend, mirror,
flatten or fill in geometry, and do not normalise varying surface depths to uniform.

presets.label: Prototype — quick print
presets.summary: Fast, coarse, disposable. Explicitly not a final part.

prompt.parametric:
INTENT PRESET: PROTOTYPE - QUICK PRINT.
Optimise for iteration latency, not for a finished part. Say so in the file.

  $fa = 6; $fs = 0.8;          // coarse on purpose - fast preview and fast render
  wall = 1.2;                  // 3 perimeters, holds its shape, half the material
  scale_factor = 1.0;          // set 0.5 to print a half-scale check article

Loose everywhere: bolt bores at the FREE fit column, moving clearances at 0.30, no
interference fits. A prototype that will not assemble teaches nothing.
Layer height 0.20-0.28 mm, infill 10-15% gyroid.

AVOID SUPPORTS by redesigning to 45 degrees rather than by adding them - support time and
removal time are most of the iteration cost. No fillets except a 0.4 mm bottom chamfer;
fillets are the slowest thing to retune and buy nothing at this stage.

Keep the code MAXIMALLY EDITABLE, because the next checkpoint will edit it: every dimension
a named variable in one block at the top, one module per feature, no repeated literals.

Add a second comment line naming exactly what was traded away, for example:
// PROTOTYPE: coarse curves ($fs=0.8), free fits (+0.30), 1.2mm walls - NOT a final part

Colour every part. Keep it manifold.

generated.image_suffix:
Single centred object, plain light background, even flat lighting, whole object in frame,
simple blocky readable forms, matte neutral grey, three-quarter view, no fine surface detail.
generated.negative:
multiple objects, background clutter, text, watermark, harsh shadows, depth of field,
fine filigree, thin protrusions, floating parts, cropped

presets.label: Strong — load bearing
presets.summary: It will be pushed, pulled, dropped or clamped.
presets.refusal_text: Generated sculpts are not dimensionally controlled — arbitrary scale, no flat mating faces, no thread or tolerance guarantees. Load-bearing and hardware-mating parts are modelled parametrically. Remove this preset to use the generator, or generate a decorative shell and branch it to add the parametric features.

prompt.parametric:
INTENT PRESET: STRONG - LOAD BEARING.
This part will be loaded. FDM is orthotropic: the Z (interlayer) direction carries only
40-75% of the XY tensile strength and 10-30% of the XY ductility. Design around that.

ORIENTATION IS THE FIRST DECISION - state it in a comment before writing geometry:
  1. Identify the primary tensile/bending axis and lay it in the bed plane (XY).
  2. A hook, bracket or cantilever prints lying on its side so bending stresses stay in-plane,
     never standing up with the load pulling layers apart.
  3. No layer boundary may coincide with the maximum-moment section. Move it or thicken 1.5x.
  4. Pins, shafts and hinge axes lie horizontal so strands run along the axis.
  5. Where Z tension is unavoidable, bridge the layers with a real fastener - do not ask the
     plastic to do it.

Sections and features:
  - minimum structural wall 2.0 mm; load-bearing sections >= 2.4 mm at 40-60% infill
  - fillet EVERY internal corner: r >= 0.5 x local wall, minimum 1.0 mm
  - chamfer the bottom outer edge 0.6 mm x 45 degrees (NOT a fillet - a bottom fillet begins
    as a >45 degree overhang); fillet bottom corners in plan view 1-3 mm against warping
  - ribs and gussets: thickness = wall, faces at <= 45 degrees so they self-support,
    spacing >= 3 x wall. Prefer ribs to solid mass.
  - force solid material around every fastener boss and bearing surface; never let a screw
    thread into infill voids.

SUPPORTLESS IS MANDATORY. Overhang budget 40 degrees (5 degrees of margin on the 45 rule).
Horizontal bores get a teardrop cross-section:
  hull() { circle(d=d); translate([0, d*0.62]) circle(d=0.6); }
Support scars are crack initiators on a load path.

Do NOT use: living hinges or thin flexure membranes in PLA (they fatigue and crack - use a
knuckle hinge with a bridged pin); sharp internal corners; rigid barbs pressed into hard
material (use a split-tip spring, slot width ~0.22 x d at ~75% depth); draft angles
(that is an injection-moulding concept and is wrong for FDM).

Set $fa = 2, $fs = 0.3. Colour every part. Keep it manifold.
If the strong orientation does not fit the 256x256 bed, check the 45-degree diagonal fit
((L + W) / sqrt(2) <= 256) and bake the rotation into the geometry - the slicer's arrange
only translates and Z-rotates, it will not reorient the part for you.

presets.label: Fits screws & parts
presets.summary: Must mate with real M-hardware or another printed part.
presets.refusal_text: Generated sculpts are not dimensionally controlled — arbitrary scale, no flat mating faces, no thread or tolerance guarantees. Load-bearing and hardware-mating parts are modelled parametrically. Remove this preset to use the generator, or generate a decorative shell and branch it to add the parametric features.

prompt.parametric:
INTENT PRESET: FITS SCREWS AND PARTS.
This part mates with real hardware or with another printed part. Dimensions are contractual.

Declare these at the top of the file and reference them everywhere - never inline a magic
number:
  hole_comp = 0.20;   // FDM bore compensation; printed holes come out undersize. 0.10 on a
                      // well-calibrated P1S with hole compensation enabled.
  tol       = 0.20;   // moving/sliding fit clearance, field-calibrated for P1S + PLA

THE INSCRIBED-POLYGON TRAP - this preset's most common silent failure: OpenSCAD's cylinder()
is INSCRIBED in the nominal diameter, so a bore drawn at d = 3.6 with $fn = 16 only passes
3.6 * cos(180/16) = 3.53 mm and an M3 will not go through. Give EVERY fastener bore
$fn = 64 (error < 0.15%), or compensate explicitly with d / cos(180/$fn).

BOLT CLEARANCE BORES - model these diameters (ISO 273 clearance + hole_comp = 0.20).
Default to the NORMAL column.
             close   normal   free
  M2         2.4     2.6      2.8
  M2.5       2.9     3.1      3.3
  M3         3.4     3.6      3.8
  M4         4.5     4.7      5.0
  M5         5.5     5.7      6.0
  M6         6.6     6.8      7.2
  M8         8.6     9.2      10.2      <- M8 breaks the pattern; do not extrapolate.
Use close only when the bolt line locates the part; use free when stacking tolerances across
two printed parts.

SOCKET-HEAD COUNTERBORE / COUNTERSINK (diameter, depth):
  M3  counterbore 6.0 x 3.2   |  90-degree countersink top dia 6.4
  M4  counterbore 7.5 x 4.2   |  90-degree countersink top dia 8.4
  M5  counterbore 9.0 x 5.2   |  90-degree countersink top dia 10.4
A counterbore ceiling bridges cleanly. A countersink in the BOTTOM face is a >45 degree
overhang - flip the part or use a counterbore instead.

HEX NUT TRAPS (pocket across-flats x depth): M3 5.7 x 2.6 | M4 7.2 x 3.4 | M5 8.2 x 4.9.
Orient a side-entry trap so its roof is a flat bridge, not an arch. 0.4 mm lead-in chamfer.

HEAT-SET INSERTS - these are pocket bores; hole_comp does NOT apply (the brass melts its own
fit). Bore / pocket depth / minimum wall around the pocket / minimum boss outer diameter:
  M2    3.4  /  4.5  / 1.5 / 6.4
  M2.5  3.8  /  6.2  / 1.5 / 6.8
  M3    4.2  /  6.2  / 1.5 / 7.2     (4.5 deep for short inserts)
  M4    5.8  /  8.6  / 2.0 / 9.8
  M5    6.6  / 10.0  / 2.5 / 11.6
  M6    8.2  / 13.2  / 2.5 / 13.2
A 1 mm x 45 degree chamfer at the pocket mouth is MANDATORY. Pocket depth = insert length
+ 0.5 mm. Prefer a through-bore so displaced plastic pushes down, not up into the threads.
PETG +0.02, ABS/ASA +0.05, nylon +0.06 on the bore.

SELF-TAPPING BOSSES (pilot / boss outer diameter / engagement depth):
  M3  2.4 / 6.6 / 7.5   |   M4  3.2 / 8.8 / 10.0   |   M5  4.0 / 11.0 / 12.5
Pilot = 0.8 x major diameter. Boss interior must be solid. Too big strips, too small cracks
the boss. A self-cut thread survives only a few assembly cycles - if the part will be opened
repeatedly, specify a heat-set insert instead and say so in the comment.

PRINTED THREADS: do not model M-threads below M6 at a 0.4 mm nozzle - the pitch is at the
extrusion width and the helix comes out ragged. For M6 and up use BOSL2 threaded_rod() /
threaded_nut() with $slop = 0.15-0.2, or a coarse trapezoidal/ACME profile for anything
turned repeatedly.

PRINTED-TO-PRINTED FITS (total diametral clearance):
  press/interference -0.05 to 0.00 (needs a lead-in chamfer; wall >= 2 mm or PLA splits)
  snug hand-assembly +0.10   |   sliding or rotating +0.20 (= tol)   |   forgiving +0.30
Print-in-place hinges use tol for BOTH the radial pin-to-sleeve gap and the axial gap
between knuckles, from one variable. Keep each pin bridge span <= 18 mm.
Magnet pockets: magnet diameter + 0.15, depth + 0.10, 0.3 mm blind ceiling.

Set $fa = 2, $fs = 0.25 globally and $fn = 64 on fastener features. Colour every part.

presets.label: Decor / organic
presets.summary: Looks matter; nothing has to fit anything.

prep.flat_cut_caveat: run_prep_stage hardcodes the cut-plane normal to +Y — this preset cannot claim the -Z face the bear/owl recipe assumes; the flat cut still lands, just not guaranteed on that face.

prompt.parametric:
INTENT PRESET: DECOR / ORGANIC.
Looks matter here; nothing in this part has to fit anything. This is the one preset where
sculptural quality outranks dimensional discipline.

Prefer BOSL2 organic-modelling primitives over hand-rolled hulls: metaballs, path_sweep(),
skin() (see openscad-organic notes). Voxel count 10,000 for preview, 50,000-100,000 for a
final render. When you do fall back to hull(), hull PAIRS of primitives, never the whole
assembly at once, and prefer cylinders over spheres inside a hull. Avoid minkowski() - it is
the slowest primitive available and organic forms rarely need it.

Resolution: $fa = 2, $fs = 0.3 - fine enough for smooth organic surfaces without the render
cost of a miniature-grade setting.

Sections: wall 1.2 mm, infill 10% (this is a decorative, not load-bearing, class of part).

Render timeout: raise it. Metaball and skin() models routinely exceed a 60 second default
render budget - say so if the render tool needs a longer timeout argument.

Colour every part with color(). Keep the model manifold; overlap coincident-height
neighbours by eps = 0.01.
prompt.parametric_provenance: COMPOSED, NOT SOURCED — intent-presets.md left §8.6 (decor-organic) as an unwritten placeholder ("INTENT PRESET: DECOR / ORGANIC. …"). This block was written by the P3 implementer from §6.5's content, in the same instructional register as the other four (verbatim) blocks. Do not treat it as pinned vault research — it has not been reviewed as such.

conflict_notes.note: Strong raises the minimum feature to 1.0 mm — sculpted detail below that will be merged or omitted.
Prototype keeps Strong's wall thickness but coarsens curves and drops infill — strength results will read low.
Strong forces the parametric track; the generator is disabled for load-bearing parts.
Sculpt first, then branch the checkpoint and difference() the mating features into the import.

_dropped_knobs: mesh --octree — no such flag on this CLI (config.toml value only); every generated preset above omits it.
prep --flat-cut face selection — the flag exists but run_prep_stage hardcodes plane_normal=(0,1,0); decor-organic ships the millimetres and a flat_cut_caveat string instead of claiming -Z.

print --profile / the entire print pipeline stage — inert on this machine (no profile JSON on disk, --load-settings absent, "print" not in PIPELINE_ACTIONS). slicer_profile stays in params as inert data for a later wave.
